briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 10, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Disasters and Warnings of Severe Impacts
sections.content: Two tornadoes that struck the western coast of Sicily today caused dozens of injuries and extensive building damage, serving as a stark reminder of the direct threat posed by the climate crisis [22]. Research warns that climate change threatens to destroy over three-quarters of the world's best surfing spots, which could disappear due to rising sea levels and coastal development [15, 23]. Furthermore, it has been reported that if global warming rises by 4℃, the majority of Japanese ski resorts will become inoperable, and climbing in the Himalayas is becoming increasingly dangerous due to its reshaping [2, 21]. Major Asian cities, including Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam, are also facing severe threats, with the city pushing for emergency restoration of 134 disaster prevention facilities due to the combined effects of land subsidence, climate change, and drainage limitations [3].

sections.title: ⚠️ Social and Psychological Dimensions of the Climate Crisis
sections.content: The climate crisis is being recognized not merely as an environmental issue but also as a psychological crisis, and widespread societal awareness of this is becoming crucial [16]. Notably, an analysis in South Korea suggests that the phenomenon of men's indifference to climate change and ESG may be linked to 'masculinity anxiety,' drawing significant attention [1]. This indicates that social approaches to promoting climate action must consider various socioeconomic factors, including gender.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts for Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Globally, efforts to transition to renewable energy for achieving carbon neutrality goals are accelerating. The UK government has approved the £224 million 'Steeple Renewable Energy Project,' attracting local investment [9]. Australia's renewable energy market is undergoing a firm transformation due to its coal phase-out policy [12], and citizen-participatory activities are also vibrant in Vietnam, with 15,000 athletes participating in the Ha Long Bay Marathon aiming to set a new carbon-neutral record [8]. Domestically, Asan City Council has commenced activities for its 'Carbon Neutrality Special Committee' [5], and Jeju Province is encouraging citizen participation through a completion event for its carbon neutrality points system in the automotive sector [6]. In Buan County, resident-led renewable energy projects are bearing fruit, with consecutive selections in the 'Sunshine Income Village' competition [11], and the Yeonggwang County Mayor has presented a vision to link renewable energy profits to residents' income [13, 14].

sections.title: 🌍 International Discussions for Strengthening Policy and Governance
sections.content: Policy and governance discussions for responding to climate change are actively taking place both domestically and internationally. Vietnamese Deputy Prime Minister Ho Quoc Dung emphasized that the 'Quy Nhon Climate Change and Transition Dialogue' must be built upon three foundations, articulating the importance of international cooperation [4]. Regarding the European Union (EU), Christian charities are urging action on climate change before COP31, demanding an active role from policymakers [18]. Domestically, Gyeonggi Provincial Council held a kick-off briefing for a study on establishing renewable energy transition action plans for 31 cities and counties, embarking on the creation of concrete regional transition plans [10]. Experts from Daegu and Gyeongbuk proposed climate crisis solutions such as 'walkable cities' and AI-based disaster prediction [7]. Furthermore, Bill Gates is targeting the aviation sector in the new war against climate change [19], and progressive economists are proposing reforms to address inequality and climate change, demonstrating a search for solutions across various fields [20].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severe impacts of the climate crisis, alongside the simultaneous multifaceted policy and technological efforts being made both domestically and internationally to overcome it. Through continued interest and cooperation, we must build a more resilient future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
